sources.entry: Logue - Privacy-first AI meeting notes and writing assistant with on-device transcription, smart minutes, action items, and 60+ writing modes — runs entirely on Apple Silicon.

summary.one_liner: Logue is a local-first macOS workspace for documents, tasks and meetings that transcribes meetings, writes minutes and runs an on-device AI agent, all on Apple Silicon via MLX.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a Notion/Obsidian-style workspace with nested spaces, a block editor, typed properties, relations, wiki links with backlinks, a document graph, saved views and 55 templates. Records meetings with real-time transcription, speaker diarization and system audio capture, then generates Smart Minutes, highlights and action items that feed a task list. An agent ("Ask Logue") uses documents, meetings, calendar, reminders and files through the app, a floating Command Center panel, or a Chrome extension. Inference, transcription and diarization run on-device via MLX; documents are encrypted at rest or can be stored as plain .md files in a folder. Optional external AI providers and web search are opt-in.
use_cases: take and transcribe meeting notes on a Mac
generate meeting minutes and action items
organise documents and tasks in a local notes workspace
chat with an on-device AI assistant over my own documents
edit writing with AI grammar and tone suggestions
keep notes as plain markdown files in a folder
how_to_run: xcodebuild build -project Logue.xcodeproj -scheme Logue -destination 'platform=macOS' CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="-" CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO
notable: Fully on-device AI via MLX on Apple Silicon, with no meeting bot joining calls
Meeting recordings resume and rebuild transcripts after disconnects or app quit
Chrome extension talks to the app over a loopback-only bridge
Plain markdown storage option that treats a ~/Logue folder as the live store
Saved views with nested filter groups and typed document properties
caveats: Requires macOS 26 (Tahoe) or later on Apple Silicon (M1 or newer) and Xcode 26+ to build
Not sandboxed, by design, so it is not App Store-style software
Documents are encrypted unless plain markdown storage is turned on; meeting data is always encrypted
